description: Package scaffold, types, AppLens singleton, storage ring-buffers, and runtime interceptors. This is the foundation FEAT — all other FEATs depend on the types and core modules created here. Creates the entire library skeleton: package.json, tsconfig.json, babel.config.js, all type files, AppLensConfig, the AppLens singleton class, MemoryStorage ring-buffer, AppLensStorage interface, NetworkInterceptor (XHR + fetch monkey-patch), and ConsoleInterceptor.

Create /Users/sunilkumar/Desktop/project/AppLens/AppLens/src/storage/MemoryStorage.ts — implements AppLensStorage. Uses three circular ring buffers (arrays with a maxSize cap, removing the oldest item when full). subscribe/unsubscribe pattern: keep Set<() => void> of listeners, call all on every mutation. All methods are synchronous.

Create /Users/sunilkumar/Desktop/project/AppLens/AppLens/src/core/AppLens.ts — singleton class (not exported as class, exported as instance). Private constructor. Public API: initialize(config: Partial<AppLensConfig>): void, getConfig(): AppLensConfig, getStorage(): AppLensStorage, trackEvent(name: string, properties?: Record<string, unknown>): void, isEnabled(): boolean. initialize() merges partial config with DEFAULT_CONFIG, starts NetworkInterceptor and ConsoleInterceptor if respective flags are true. getStorage() returns the MemoryStorage instance. The singleton is exported as both the default export and a named export: export { AppLens }. AppLens.initialize must be idempotent — second call updates config but does not re-attach interceptors if already attached.

Create /Users/sunilkumar/Desktop/project/AppLens/AppLens/src/interceptors/NetworkInterceptor.ts — monkey-patches global XMLHttpRequest and global fetch. For XHR: override open() to capture method+url, override send() to capture body + start timer, override onload/onerror to capture status, headers, response, duration. For fetch: wrap global.fetch to capture all the same fields. On each request start, call storage.addNetworkRequest() with state 'pending'. On completion, call storage.updateNetworkRequest() with status, headers, body, duration, state 'complete' or 'error'. Redact headers listed in config.redactHeaders (case-insensitive match) by replacing value with '[REDACTED]'. Truncate request/response bodies at 50KB to avoid memory pressure. attach() and detach() methods. Never intercept requests to AppLens own AI endpoint (check url includes 'api.openai.com' — these should still be captured but their Authorization header must be redacted). Export class NetworkInterceptor.

Create /Users/sunilkumar/Desktop/project/AppLens/AppLens/src/interceptors/ConsoleInterceptor.ts — saves references to original console.log/info/warn/error/debug. Replaces each with a wrapper that: calls the original (so dev console still works), captures a LogEntry with id (uuid via Math.random), level, message (String(args[0])), args, timestamp: Date.now(), stack (via new Error().stack, trimmed to remove the interceptor frame). Stores in AppLensStorage. attach() and detach() methods. Export class ConsoleInterceptor.

findings: 1. @react-native/typescript-config base tsconfig uses moduleResolution:bundler + customConditions which conflicts with overriding to moduleResolution:node — wrote a standalone tsconfig instead of extending the base. 2. React Native types use HeadersInit_ (not HeadersInit) and XHR.open only accepts string url (not URL) — interceptors use narrowed types and 'any' casts for prototype overrides. 3. @types/react and @types/react-native added as devDependencies (not in spec but required for tsc --noEmit to pass). 4. global.fetch type in RN has three overloads including URL variant — wrapper function signature updated to accept RequestInfo | URL.
